python3 -c 'exec("""import os, json, duckdb, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
os.makedirs("out", exist_ok=True)
query = "select extract(year from crash_date)::int as year, sum(coalesce(number_of_motorist_killed, 0))::int as motorist_deaths, sum(coalesce(number_of_cyclist_killed, 0))::int as cyclist_deaths from read_parquet(?) where extract(year from crash_date) between 2013 and 2025 group by 1 order by 1"
data = duckdb.connect().execute(query, ["data/crashes.parquet"]).df()
assert data["year"].tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
data.to_csv("out/values_1.csv", index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.8))
x = range(len(data)); width = 0.38
bars_m = ax.bar([v-width/2 for v in x], data.motorist_deaths, width, label="Motorists", color="#326891")
bars_c = ax.bar([v+width/2 for v in x], data.cyclist_deaths, width, label="Cyclists", color="#e07a3f")
ax.bar_label(bars_m, padding=2, fontsize=8); ax.bar_label(bars_c, padding=2, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xticks(list(x), data.year.astype(str)); ax.set_ylabel("People killed (annual count)")
ax.set_title("Motorist and cyclist deaths in NYC crashes, 2013–2025")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncols=2, loc="upper left"); ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(data.motorist_deaths)*1.18); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("out/option_1.png", dpi=180); plt.close(fig)
diff = data[["year"]].copy(); diff["motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths"] = data.motorist_deaths - data.cyclist_deaths
diff.to_csv("out/values_2.csv", index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.8))
colors = ["#326891" if value >= 0 else "#e07a3f" for value in diff.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths]
bars = ax.bar(diff.year.astype(str), diff.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths, color=colors, width=0.68)
ax.bar_label(bars, padding=3, fontsize=9); ax.axhline(0, color="#444444", linewidth=0.9)
ax.set_ylabel("More motorist than cyclist deaths")
ax.set_title("Annual gap in deaths: motorists minus cyclists, NYC, 2013–2025")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False); ax.set_ylim(0, max(diff.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths)*1.17)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("out/option_2.png", dpi=180); plt.close(fig)
options = {"options": [
{"id": 1, "metric": "Annual deaths among motorists and cyclists", "denominator": "None; absolute summed deaths", "grouping": "Year and road-user group", "chart_type": "Grouped bar chart", "reason": "Side-by-side annual counts show both the scale and year-to-year pattern for each group.", "probability": 0.7, "answer": "Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year; motorist deaths ranged from 72 to 139 annually, while cyclist deaths ranged from 10 to 31.", "interpretation": "This framing answers the question by showing each group’s annual death count side by side, and the chart shows a higher motorist count in all 13 years. Absolute counts are a direct comparison of deaths recorded in these crash data. It leaves differences in population or travel exposure unaddressed."},
{"id": 2, "metric": "Motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths per year", "denominator": "None; absolute count difference", "grouping": "Year", "chart_type": "Bar chart of annual count differences", "reason": "The annual difference makes the size and direction of the gap easy to compare across years.", "probability": 0.3, "answer": "Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year, with the gap ranging from 51 deaths in 2019 to 115 in 2021.", "interpretation": "This framing answers how far apart the annual death counts were, and every bar is positive, indicating more motorist than cyclist deaths in each year. The count difference is a defensible summary of the comparison, especially for seeing when the gap widened or narrowed. It leaves the separate annual totals and any exposure-adjusted risk comparison less explicit."}
]}
with open("out/options.json", "w") as f: json.dump(options, f, indent=2); f.write("\n")
print(data.to_string(index=False)); print(diff.to_string(index=False))
""")'
